newsitem.title: USA: Spending on construction up 1.9 percent in November.
newsitem.headline: Spending on construction up 1.9 percent in November.

text.p: Spending on new construction climbed at the fastest pace in eight months in November, the Commerce Department said Friday, new evidence that building activity approached the end of the year at a healthy level.
Total spending rose 1.9 percent in the month to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of $592 billion following a revised increase of 1.5 percent in October.
Public construction spending on projects like sewers, water treatment plants and highways jumped 2.5 percent in November to $150.3 billion after rising 1.9 percent in October.
Privately financed construction was up 1.7 percent in November to $441.6 billion after rising 1.4 percent in October.
Spending by contractors on new homes and apartments rose 1.2 percent while construction of nonresidential buildings like new office buildings and plants increased 1.6 percent.
The latest data reinforced earlier reports showing both existing homes and new single family dwellings were selling well during November.
Previously, the department said October construction spending rose 1.8 percent. After allowing for inflation, total construction spending increased 1.7 percent after rising 1.4 percent in October.
The November rate was the biggest jump in construction spending since the 2.3 percent increase last March, the department said.
